title: Exertional rhabdomyolysis, 55-year-old marathon runner (the 2026-09-30 baseline case)
provenance: Vignette written 2026-09-30 for the evaluation harness; expected answers extracted from the cited documents.

intake.complaint: Severe bilateral lower extremity pain, generalised muscle weakness, and dark tea-coloured urine for two days.

triage.note: Both extractors: level 3. A: Only GCS 15 and pain score 7 are recorded. Adult vital-signs table p7: 'Pain Score 4 - 7' sits in the x~244 column = Level 3 (Severe Pain 8-10 is Level 2 at x~131). Limb pain/swelling complaint p10: 'Not able to bear weight' is Level 3 (x~244); primary triage p4 'Cannot sit / stand unsupported' is Level 3 (x~350). No HR/BP/RR/SpO2/temperature are given; tachycardia >120, SBP<90, temp >39 or GCS drop would upgrade to Level 2, and a suspected compartment syndrome is a Level 2 cell in primary-triage Bleeding (p5, x~246). Hence acceptable [2,3]. B: Only GCS 15 and pain score 7 are recorded. Pain 7 is in the Level 3 cell of adult vital signs (p7, x~244); Severe Pain (8-10) would be Level 2. Complaint cells that apply: Limb pain row Level 3 'Not able to bear weight' (p10, x~244) and Genito-urinary Level 3 'Frank haematuria' (p9, x~244) if the tea-coloured urine counts as haematuria; primary triage Level 3 'Cannot sit / stand unsupported' (p4, x~350) if he cannot stand. HR, BP, RR, SpO2 and temperature are missing: HR > 120, SBP < 90 or Temp > 39 would each make it Level 2 (p7, x~131), and a cold, dusky, pulseless limb (compartment syndrome) would give Limb pain Level 2 (p10, x~131). So 3 is expected and 2 is defensible.

disposition.note: Revised 2026-10-03 under the KKM-only source policy. The earlier key (ADMIT_WARD/ADMIT_ICU_HDU only) rested entirely on CHAMP USUHS 2020, which left the index on 2026-09-30. No indexed KKM document states an admission criterion for exertional rhabdomyolysis; the Patient Flow Guideline 2022 says admission is decided against the hospital's own criteria with the specialist (p19, p4). ED_OBSERVATION pending CK/renal/potassium is therefore acceptable when the report says that decision is open (rag_engine._admission_process_note). Admission remains preferred: two days of dark urine with severe pain needs IV fluids and serial CK. DISCHARGE_WITH_FOLLOW_UP and REFER_SPECIALIST stay unacceptable - high-risk markers cannot be excluded at triage.

adjudication.method: two independent extraction passes (A, B); agreed items scored

A: KKM corpus has no exertional-rhabdomyolysis guidance; nearly all management items rely on the non-KKM CHAMP/USUHS (military) and AAST documents. The MOH Heat Related Illness 2016 guideline is heat-stroke specific; its investigation list (CK, urine myoglobin, K, Ca, renal function) was reused as KKM corroboration.

Sodium bicarbonate: AAST says bicarbonate (and diuretics) for AKI prevention is not recommended, while CHAMP allows optional urine alkalinisation for positive urine myoglobin or metabolic acidosis. Not listed as forbidden; adjudicator to decide.
CHAMP says hypocalcaemia should only be treated with dysrhythmia or seizures (routine calcium replacement discouraged); not listed as a forbidden drug because it is conditional.
Pain score 7: MOH Pain Management in ETD calls 7-10 severe (IV morphine), while MTS puts 7 in Level 3 (4-7). Triage used MTS; analgesia item cites both.
B: KKM documents have no exertional rhabdomyolysis guidance; most items rely on the non-KKM CHAMP/USUHS and AAST copies. The MOH Heat Related Illness 2016 guideline supports only the CK/urine myoglobin investigations and the heat-stroke differential.

Bicarbonate: AAST says it is not recommended for AKI prevention, but CHAMP (p18) allows optional urine alkalinisation when there is myoglobinuria or acidosis. I marked it forbidden with required=false; the adjudicator may prefer to drop it.
Triage is under-specified because the intake has no HR/BP/RR/SpO2/temperature; 2 is in 'acceptable' for that reason.
